BiblicalUsage: The shearing house is all the name gives us — Beth-Eked means house of binding, the place where sheep were sheared — and it appears only while Jehu is passing through on his bloody errand. In 2 Kings 10:12 he comes to the shearing house on the way to Samaria, and in 2 Kings 10:14 he seizes Ahab's kinsmen there and has them killed at the pit. A working place, a sheep-shearing stop, turned into a place of slaughter.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the shearing house reminds me that judgment can fall in the most ordinary places, right in the middle of the day's work.
